newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal and soyoil end mostly down on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal and soyoil end mostly down on weather.

text.p: CBOT soymeal and soyoil futures ended mostly lower on Thursday, following soybeans, amid forecasts for rain next week in central Illinois, traders said.
"Soy products are pretty much tagging along with soybeans," a veteran oilseeds trader said. "There's not much independent movement in those pits right now."

Forecasters disagreed on how much rain would reach dry pockets of central Illinois next week but Weather Express Chief Forecaster Fred Gesser predicted widespread rainfall would reach the dry areas on Monday.

"Moisture from what should become Tropical Storm Danny is in a position to provide 0.50 to 2.00-plus inches with 80 percent coverage for Missouri and southern Illinois up to Peoria on Monday," Gesser said.

The soy complex had rallied on Monday after rains bypassed portions of central Illinois and eastern Iowa. Those areas have been hit with persistent hot, dry weather which can be damaging to developing crops.
Soymeal ended down $4.10 per ton to up $1.50 with December off $3.00 at $193.30. Soyoil closed down 0.21 to 0.14 cent per lb with December down 0.14 at 22.46.
July soymeal bucked the trend, ending higher on a lack of deliveries posted. No deliveries are expected as cash meal continues to trade at a premium to futures.
Traders also pointed to expectations of a low weekly crush figure, meaning lower supplies of soymeal and soyoil.

The National Oilseed Processors Association will release its weekly crush data early Friday. Trade sources expected the report to show between 21.5 and 22.8 million bushels of soybeans crushed, compared with 23 million the previous week.
On the day, commercials were small-lot buyers of old crop soymeal. Cargill Inc bought 400 August, Continental Grain bought 300 August and ADM bought 100 August, traders said.
Smith Barney sold 400 August and 100 December.
In spread action, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer spread 600 lots August/December at $48.00 to $49.00, premium August. LIT spread 200 August/September at $22.50, premium August.
In soyoil, trade was thin. Pit sources said Smith Barney bought 300 December while ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp and Cargill Investor Services each sold 200 December.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 21,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 21,062 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 13,000 lots, against Wednesday's 13,808.
